-- this theorem might be useful in the proof of the problem
theorem exists_deriv_eq_zero {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
  (hab : a < b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hfI : f a = f b) :
  ∃ c ∈ Set.Ioo a b, deriv f c = 0

-- here's an example of theorem exists_deriv_eq_zero being used
example (p : ℝ[X]) :
    p.roots.toFinset.card ≤ (p.derivative.roots.toFinset \ p.roots.toFinset).card + 1 := by
  rcases eq_or_ne (derivative p) 0 with hp' | hp'
  · rw [eq_C_of_derivative_eq_zero hp', roots_C, Multiset.toFinset_zero, Finset.card_empty]
    exact zero_le _
  have hp : p ≠ 0 := ne_of_apply_ne derivative (by rwa [derivative_zero])
  refine Finset.card_le_diff_of_interleaved fun x hx y hy hxy hxy' => ?_
  rw [Multiset.mem_toFinset, mem_roots hp] at hx hy
  obtain ⟨z, hz1, hz2⟩ := exists_deriv_eq_zero hxy p.continuousOn (hx.trans hy.symm)
  refine ⟨z, ?_, hz1⟩
  rwa [Multiset.mem_toFinset, mem_roots hp', IsRoot, ← p.deriv]

-- this theorem might be useful in the proof of the problem
theorem ContinuousOn.mono {f : α → β} {s t : Set α}
  (hf : ContinuousOn f s) (h : t ⊆ s) : ContinuousOn f t

-- here's an example of theorem ContinuousOn.mono being used
example {r : ℝ} {s : Set ℝ≥0} (h : 0 ∉ s ∨ 0 ≤ r) :
    ContinuousOn (fun z : ℝ≥0 => z ^ r) s := by
  refine h.elim ?_ ?_
  · intro hs
    exact ContinuousOn.mono (s := {0}ᶜ) (by fun_prop) (by aesop)
  · intro hr
    exact (NNReal.continuous_rpow_const hr).continuousOn

theorem QuotientAddGroup.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective
  (φ : G →+ H) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) :
  G ⧸ φ.ker ≃+ H

-- here's an example of theorem QuotientAddGroup.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective being used
example {G : Type*} [AddGroup G] (h : IsAddCyclic G) :
    ZMod (Nat.card G) ≃+ G := by
  let n := Nat.card G
  let ⟨g, surj⟩ := Classical.indefiniteDescription _ h.exists_generator
  have kereq : ((zmultiplesHom G) g).ker = zmultiples ↑(Nat.card G) := by
    rw [zmultiplesHom_ker_eq]
    congr
    rw [← Nat.card_zmultiples]
    exact Nat.card_congr (Equiv.subtypeUnivEquiv surj)
  exact Int.quotientZMultiplesNatEquivZMod n
    |>.symm.trans <| QuotientAddGroup.quotientAddEquivOfEq kereq
    |>.symm.trans <| QuotientAddGroup.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective (zmultiplesHom G g) surj

theorem Monoid.exists_orderOf_eq_exponent {G : Type u} [CommMonoid G]
  (hG : Monoid.ExponentExists G) : ∃ g, orderOf g = Monoid.exponent G

-- here's an example of theorem Monoid.exists_orderOf_eq_exponent being used
example {G : Type*} [CommMonoid G] (h : ∀ g : G, 0 < orderOf g) :
    Monoid.exponent G = ⨆ g : G, orderOf g := by
  rw [iSup]
  by_cases hE : Monoid.ExponentExists G
  · rw [csSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt (Set.range_nonempty _)]
    · simp_rw [Set.mem_range, forall_exists_index, forall_apply_eq_imp_iff]
      exact Monoid.orderOf_le_exponent hE
    · intro x hx
      obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := Monoid.exists_orderOf_eq_exponent (G := G) hE
      rw [← hg] at hx
      exact ⟨g, hx⟩
  · rw [← Monoid.exponent_eq_zero_iff] at hE
    rw [hE, Set.Infinite.Nat.sSup_eq_zero]
    exact (Monoid.exponent_eq_zero_iff_range_orderOf_infinite h).1 hE

theorem Monoid.order_dvd_exponent {G : Type u} [Monoid G]
  (g : G) : orderOf g ∣ Monoid.exponent G

example {ι G : Type*} [Finite ι] [CommGroup G] {n : ι → ℕ}
    (e : G ≃* ((i : ι) → Multiplicative (ZMod (n i)))) (i : ι) :
    n i ∣ Monoid.exponent G := by
  classical
  have h_order : n i = orderOf (e.symm <| Pi.mulSingle i <| Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) := by
    simpa only [MulEquiv.orderOf_eq, orderOf_piMulSingle, orderOf_ofAdd_eq_addOrderOf]
      using (ZMod.addOrderOf_one (n i)).symm
  exact h_order ▸ Monoid.order_dvd_exponent _

-- this theorem might be useful in the proof of the problem
theorem Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_eq_multiplicity
  (p : Polynomial R) (a : R) :
  Polynomial.rootMultiplicity a p =
    if p = 0 then 0 else multiplicity (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) p

-- here's an example of theorem Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_eq_multiplicity being used
example [CommRing R] [DecidableEq R] {p : R[X]} {x : R} :
    Polynomial.rootMultiplicity x p = 0 ↔ Polynomial.IsRoot p x → p = 0 := by
  classical
  simp only [Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_eq_multiplicity, ite_eq_left_iff,
    Nat.cast_zero, multiplicity_eq_zero, Polynomial.dvd_iff_isRoot, not_imp_not]

-- this theorem might be useful in the proof of the problem
theorem Polynomial.exists_eq_pow_rootMultiplicity_mul_and_not_dvd
  (p : Polynomial R) (hp : p ≠ 0) (a : R) :
  ∃ q, p = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ Polynomial.rootMultiplicity a p * q
    ∧ ¬ Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a ∣ q

-- here's an example of theorem Polynomial.exists_eq_pow_rootMultiplicity_mul_and_not_dvd being used
example {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [Ring S] [Algebra R S]
    {s : S} (hRs : IsAlgebraic R s) (hs : s ∈ nonZeroDivisors S) :
    ∃ q : R[X], q.coeff 0 ≠ 0 ∧ aeval s q = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp0, hp⟩ := hRs
  obtain ⟨q, hpq, hq⟩ := Polynomial.exists_eq_pow_rootMultiplicity_mul_and_not_dvd p hp0 0
  simp only [Polynomial.C_0, sub_zero, Polynomial.X_pow_mul, Polynomial.X_dvd_iff] at hpq hq
  rw [hpq, map_mul, Polynomial.aeval_X_pow] at hp
  exact ⟨q, hq, (nonZeroDivisors S).pow_mem hs (Polynomial.rootMultiplicity 0 p) (aeval s q) hp⟩

theorem Polynomial.dvd_iff_isRoot :
  Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a ∣ p ↔ p.IsRoot a

example [CommRing R] {p : R[X]} {a : R} :
